name: JobSearchShortlist

custom.system_prompt: You are generating conversations which focus on job searching.

initial_prompt: Create a collaborative conversation that focuses on finding the right job, including users preferences and exploring multiple opportunities.

variations.context: Working through a job-application shortlist together

setting.relationship_dynamic: Partners, one job-hunting and one helping
setting.background: A shortlist of roles built up over the week, none a perfect fit
setting.conversation_style: Practical and honest, with some encouragement

scenario_template.topic: Reviewing which roles are worth applying for
scenario_template.note: They go through a shortlist built up over the week

scenario_template.topic: The listings all want more experience than one of them has
scenario_template.note: The gap between the job description and the CV is the sticking point
They work out which past work actually maps onto the role

scenario_template.topic: Tightening the CV for one specific listing
scenario_template.note: They decide what to cut and what to lead with

scenario_template.topic: Whether to apply now or wait for a better fit
scenario_template.note: Neither is certain; they argue both sides

scenario_template.topic: Setting a deadline for the application
scenario_template.note: They agree who does what before the weekend
The mood settles; talk drifts elsewhere

user1.name: User1
user1.role: Person who is motivated to find a suitable job but has limited experience with job searching and can become overwhelmed when faced with many listings, application requirements, unfamiliar roles, or competing priorities.

user2.name: User2
user2.role: Person who is organized and detail-oriented, willing to help manage the job search, but tends to overthink opportunities, compare positions extensively, double-check application materials, and seek confirmation before applying.

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.role: Job search assistant that provides clear, structured, and practical guidance for identifying suitable opportunities, evaluating job descriptions, prioritizing applications, improving resumes and application materials, and adapting the search strategy when experience, location, salary, or other constraints limit available options.
